source: Original items, not a reproduction of any copyrighted scale. Written against the trait taxonomy documented in Bhagavad-Gita chapters 14, 17 & 18 and summarized in Dasa, D.G. (1999), 'The Vedic Personality Inventory,' Bhaktivedanta College — the same primary description the published VPI (Wolf, 1999) was itself built from. Traits covered: Sattva (cleanliness, truthfulness, gravity, dutifulness, detachment, discipline, mental equilibrium, contentment, sense control, determination); Rajas (intense activity, desire for sense gratification, dissatisfaction, envy, materialistic mentality); Tamas (mental imbalance, anger, ignorance, arrogance, depression, laziness, procrastination, helplessness).

items.text: I keep my surroundings and habits clean and orderly.
I find it easy to speak the truth, even when it's uncomfortable.
I take my duties and responsibilities seriously.
I stay calm and steady in success or failure.
I can let go of things I want, without resentment, when it's right to do so.
I keep a disciplined daily routine.
I feel generally content with my life as it is.
I can resist impulses that I know aren't good for me.
Once I decide something is right, I follow through with determination.
I think clearly and see situations for what they are, without much distortion.
I naturally treat people with respect, regardless of their status.
I feel a quiet sense of inner balance most days.
I'm often driven by a strong desire to get more out of life.
I find it hard to sit still or slow down.
I care a lot about seeking pleasure and enjoyable experiences.
I'm rarely satisfied with what I currently have or have achieved.
I notice envy when others have something I want.
Material success and status matter a great deal to me.
I'm often preoccupied with my next goal rather than the present moment.
I get restless if I'm not actively working toward something.
I have little patience for slowing down to reflect on spiritual or inner matters.
I push myself hard, even at the cost of rest or wellbeing.
My mood rises and falls a lot with how things are going for me.
I feel a persistent restlessness underneath, even in calm moments.
My mind often feels foggy, confused, or hard to focus.
I get angry more easily than I'd like to admit.
I procrastinate on things I know I should be doing.
I often feel low, heavy, or without much motivation.
I feel helpless to change my situation, even when I'd like to.
I tend to overestimate myself or dismiss others' views without good reason.
I sleep excessively or feel drowsy during the day.
I avoid facing problems rather than working through them.
I feel stuck in old habits, even ones that don't serve me.
I lose track of what's really going on around me.
I let carelessness or laziness get in the way of my responsibilities.
I feel a general sense of dullness or lack of clarity about my life direction.

scoring_notes: 12 items per guna, no reverse-scored items (matches the original VPI design, which found each guna reliably separable without reverse items). Score = sum of the 12 items / 12 (1-6 range, no neutral midpoint) per guna. Convert to a percentage-of-total for display: guna% = (guna_score / (sattva_score + rajas_score + tamas_score)) * 100, so the three percentages sum to 100 — this is the standard VPI reporting convention.
